synthesis.body: Appending a row to a markdown table that is followed by a blank line puts the new row *after* the blank, which terminates the table -- the row renders as literal pipe-delimited text. It happened twice in one change (D46, then D47). A `grep '^| D46'` Done-when check passes either way because the bytes are present. Assert adjacency to the previous row instead, or parse the table.

title: A blank line silently ends a markdown table, and a row-presence grep still passes
